A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaX research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including v2's added Appendix B and checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet pre-training, C4 language-model pre-training, and arithmetic and commonsense fine-tuning results, alongside gate/rank comparisons and training curves.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds component analyses and ablation results in Appendix B, Tables 19–23.

M1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a tested Tensor Train variant with a CoLA-style nonlinearity after the down projection, including its combination with LaX. This is a limited architectural extension; the original latent-crossing equations, gates, and normalization procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K, C4, Math10K with six arithmetic evaluation tasks, and eight commonsense reasoning tasks. Appendix B investigates model components within the existing vision setting, without adding datasets, domains, or distinct input scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 20 adds Tensor Train with CoLA-style activation but without LaX as a comparator for the corresponding LaX variant. The comparison methods in the original benchmark tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces controlled experiments varying inter-/intra-layer pathways, normalization, nonlinearities, and layer placement, plus inspection of an existing rank-256 checkpoint. The original experimental protocols and Appendix A hyperparameters are retained; B.2 explicitly reuses Table 1's training setup.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's gate/rank comparisons and training curves, Appendix B adds layerwise gate analysis, interaction with nonlinear TT activations, separate inter-/intra-layer ablations, LayerNorm removal, and layer-placement ablations. These substantially expand evidence about component contributions and training failure.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly explains that compute constraints prevent multiple pre-training runs for all variants and explicitly acknowledges absent statistical-significance reporting. This adds replication information, but no exact run counts, seeds, error bars, or confidence intervals, and does not establish a change in runs performed.

E6.justification: The original benchmark scores are unchanged, but Tables 19–23 add substantial component-level findings. Newly reported results include 77.73% accuracy for TT with CoLA-style activation and LaX, 73.87% versus 73.25% for inter-only versus intra-only TT pathways, and NaN loss with 0.10% accuracy after removing LayerNorm. These concern added configurations, not improved scores for retained configurations.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Section 3 and complexity expressions in Tables 3–4 are unchanged. Appendix B adds empirical analyses and interpretations, without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about LaX improving low-rank vision/language pre-training and LoRA fine-tuning with little overhead. The added analyses provide supporting evidence without redefining the headline contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B substantially expands the mechanistic discussion: gate magnitudes are interpreted as component reliance, nonlinear TT and LaX are described as synergistic, and pathway/placement results motivate component-specific guidance. It also attributes failure without LayerNorm to activation drift and gradient instability. The checklist newly acknowledges replication constraints.

D1.justification: Checklist item 7 newly reports approximately 450 A100 GPU-hours for one SVD-based ViT-B pre-training run. Appendix B identifies the checkpoint and reused setup for particular analyses. The existing code link and Appendix A implementation and hyperparameter information are retained.

R1.justification: The same 67 works and related-work positioning are retained. Reference [22] receives publication and author-name metadata updates, which do not introduce a different cited work.

P1.justification: v2 appends Appendix B and the NeurIPS checklist, adds a pointer to the new experiments, and updates the conference footer and bibliographic metadata. The existing narrative and section organization are otherwise essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Five compact tables are added for the new analyses. The nine existing figures and original table structures are retained, with limited alignment and spacing adjustments and reference pagination changes; there is no extensive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Appendix B improves support for design choices by isolating pathway, placement, and normalization effects and testing the nonlinear TT extension. The compute-cost and replication disclosures improve transparency. The overall gain is limited: the central benchmark evidence remains unchanged, and the added results still lack uncertainty quantification.
